scope: Synthetic-only tests for privacy audit sensitivity and fail-closed boundaries
execution_rule: Every result must bind the exact build, config, tool versions, fixture digest, observer vantage point, and limitations. A planned control is not a test result.

controls.name: Canary plaintext escape
controls.precondition: Use a synthetic test identity and unique fake message-body canary in a controlled local test.
controls.injected_condition: The primary test exercises the normal path. A separate deliberately broken harness fixture writes the canary to a fake service-side log.
controls.expected_secure_result: No canary plaintext appears in service-side delivery telemetry or unexpected egress. Explicit endpoint-local plaintext display is outside this specific assertion and must be separately scoped.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: The deliberately broken fixture must be detected by the exact scanning harness.
controls.on_failure: Fail the scoped privacy claim; preserve only the minimized synthetic trace.
controls.claim_limit: Passing a local canary test does not prove remote server retention behavior or all possible code paths.

controls.name: Recipient identifier egress
controls.precondition: Use synthetic recipient identifiers and a controlled test endpoint.
controls.injected_condition: Instrument request metadata and create one known-bad fixture that adds a direct recipient identifier to a query parameter or header.
controls.expected_secure_result: Only fields declared necessary by the frozen profile are transmitted; undeclared direct identifiers are absent or the action fails closed.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: The known-bad fixture must be detected.
controls.on_failure: Fail the selected metadata minimization claim and open a path-specific remediation.
controls.claim_limit: An absence in one endpoint capture says nothing about other routes or remote logs.

controls.name: Low-entropy identifier enumeration demonstration
controls.precondition: Use a small synthetic namespace of fake phone/email-like identifiers; no real contact data.
controls.injected_condition: Compare plain truncating hash lookup against a configured privacy-preserving protocol profile; also test repeated oracle queries and invalid/over-budget token redemptions.
controls.expected_secure_result: The test reports separately what each role learns, whether enumeration is possible under the frozen query budget, and which collusion/transport assumptions are required. No anonymity Boolean is emitted.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: The naive-hash baseline must demonstrate the expected synthetic dictionary-recovery risk; abuse-control bypass mutants must be caught.
controls.on_failure: No contact-discovery privacy promotion; route issues through existing Mycelix PSI work #2297.
controls.claim_limit: Passing this synthetic suite does not prove malicious-secure PSI, anonymity, traffic-analysis resistance, or protection against all collusion.

controls.name: Key-directory equivocation and stale mapping
controls.precondition: Use two synthetic clients and a controlled fake key directory.
controls.injected_condition: Return different account-to-key mappings to the two clients, then replay a stale prior mapping and a valid but newly enrolled device mapping.
controls.expected_secure_result: The client never labels a mapping verified when the selected profile cannot establish consistency/currentness; conflicts and unsupported states stay visible.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: A deliberately broken client that trusts the directory's positive Boolean must be detected.
controls.on_failure: Fail the key authenticity claim; do not represent key transparency as proof of real-world identity.
controls.claim_limit: A synthetic equivocation test does not establish a production transparency log or prevent endpoint compromise/account takeover.

controls.name: Diagnostic export redaction
controls.precondition: Use a synthetic crash/report fixture containing fake credentials, fake recipient ID and canary message content.
controls.injected_condition: Request a diagnostic package through the supported export boundary; include one deliberately unsafe exporter variant.
controls.expected_secure_result: Sensitive fields are removed or the export is blocked, and the user can inspect the exact payload before any upload.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: The deliberately unsafe exporter must be detected by the archive inspector.
controls.on_failure: Block diagnostic upload/promotion until the path is fixed or explicitly scoped.
controls.claim_limit: This does not prove third-party support systems delete files after a user submits them.

controls.name: Backup deletion and stale-device semantics
controls.precondition: Use a synthetic account, fake message canary and an explicitly selected local test backup target.
controls.injected_condition: Create backup, delete/tombstone source, revoke a device, restore on a fresh test device and attempt rollback to an older backup.
controls.expected_secure_result: The restore outcome states precisely which content is restored, which deletions/revocations survive, and what recovery limitations apply; no silent claim that every copy is erased.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: A known-bad fixture that falsely reports complete erasure or re-authorizes a revoked device must be detected.
controls.on_failure: Fail the corresponding backup/revocation claim and preserve the minimized synthetic fixture.
controls.claim_limit: Local backup testing does not prove deletion from all remote or user-made copies.

controls.name: Conflicting provider identity and native projection
controls.precondition: Use a frozen synthetic provider event corpus with explicit provenance and audience rules.
controls.injected_condition: Reuse a provider event ID with conflicting semantic commitment; mutate actor attribution, edit/delete lineage, audience or receipt field.
controls.expected_secure_result: Conflicting identity is preserved as conflict/rejected, and provider authorship, membership, delivery and receipt are not promoted into native Pulse authority.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: A deliberately permissive projection must be rejected.
controls.on_failure: Block affected bridge route; do not publish outbound effects.
controls.claim_limit: Passing synthetic mapping cases does not qualify a live provider integration or lossless interoperability.

controls.name: Unsupported schema and unknown metadata field
controls.precondition: Use synthetic serialized records under a frozen schema version.
controls.injected_condition: Add unknown authority-bearing fields, unsupported enum values, conflicting duplicate keys, missing required fields, and future schema versions.
controls.expected_secure_result: Unknown or unsupported input cannot construct a trusted positive state; it yields explicit unsupported/conflict/invalid evidence.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: A deliberately permissive parser or status constructor must be caught.
controls.on_failure: Fail schema/protocol qualification for the affected version.
controls.claim_limit: A strict deserializer does not establish cryptographic validity or remote authorization.

controls.name: Timing and size correlation experiment
controls.precondition: Run paired sessions using fully synthetic senders, recipients, group patterns and payload classes in a controlled lab.
controls.injected_condition: Change one feature at a time: message size, time, route, retry, group event or device presence. Compare observer traces under the exact proposed mitigation profile.
controls.expected_secure_result: Report distinguishability, confidence, sample limits, false positives/negatives and residual leakage. Do not claim anonymity from a non-significant result.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: A known timing/size marker must be detected in the baseline variant to demonstrate observer sensitivity.
controls.on_failure: Document the leak and decide on minimization, padding, batching, delayed delivery or explicit non-protection under a named threat model.
controls.claim_limit: This is an empirical side-channel assessment, not proof of traffic-analysis resistance.

controls.name: Privacy-preserving rate limit without stable redemption identity
controls.precondition: Use a synthetic issuer, test origin and contact-discovery endpoint.
controls.injected_condition: Replay one token, exceed query budget, redeem for the wrong origin/epoch and test issuance/redemption correlation under separately-operated issuer/origin profiles.
controls.expected_secure_result: Unauthorized or over-budget queries fail; report exactly which collusion and trust assumptions are required to prevent linkage.
controls.harness_sensitivity_gate: Token replay, cross-origin and budget-amplification mutants must be detected.
controls.on_failure: Do not enable bulk/private contact discovery; reuse the existing PSI composition work.
controls.claim_limit: A privacy-preserving token does not by itself prove transport privacy, anonymous contact discovery or malicious security.
